newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CBA SAYS MARGIN PRESSURE TO CONTINUE.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CBA SAYS MARGIN PRESSURE TO CONTINUE.

text.p: Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CBA) said on Wednesday that it expected pressure on its margins to continue and that its cost structure would stay under pressure because of wage rises and technology costs.
"Competition in all markets is likely to remain keen," the bank said in a statement accompanying its annual results.
"Pressure on margins will continue, heightened by the flow through of the significant reductions to home loan margins during 1996/97 and government policy on pensioner deeming rates," the bank said.
CBA earlier reported a net profit of A$1.078 billion for the year to June 30, down slightly from A$1.119 billion a year earlier.

"The bank's cost structure will remain under pressure from labour unit cost increments, year 2000 systems modifications and continuing reinvestment in distribution systems and new businesses," it said.
The CBA said general credit quality remained sound and bad debt expense was expected to remain cyclically low.

"However, a slowing in writebacks suggests that the overall bad debt expense is not likely to decrease any further," it said. "Directors see no reason why a relatively strong payout ratio cannot be maintained for the time being."
The bank paid an annual dividend of A$1.02 per share, up from 90 cents a year earlier.
